description: kubementat version-freshness config. Every default version is owned by exactly one file, `src/kubementat/core/assets/versions.yaml`, and every custom manager below reads that file. What this file carries per key is the other half of the pin: the datasource that answers a newer version, its registry, and how bumps group into pull requests. Python dependencies and their lock file stay under the native pep621 manager (with weekly lock-file maintenance, which shells out to uv and so needs the renovate -full image), and the workflows' action pins stay under the native GitHub Actions manager: those are the only pins outside versions.yaml. All managers here version with semver-coerced, because the file keeps versions as they are consumed — v-prefixes, build metadata, edge releases and channel tags coexist and order as one kind of string.

lockFileMaintenance.description: refresh uv.lock weekly through the pep621 manager, which shells out to uv — so the runner must use the renovate -full image

customManagers.description: helm chart pin — prometheus-community/prometheus: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — prometheus-community/prometheus-blackbox-exporter: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — sstarcher/helm-exporter: its version carries build metadata, which semver-coerced orders correctly
helm chart pin — grafana-community/grafana: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — grafana-community/loki: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — grafana/alloy: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — fairwinds-stable/polaris: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — jetstack/cert-manager: the pin carries the upstream v-prefix, which semver-coerced accepts and strips for comparison
helm chart pin — traefik/traefik: the chart's appVersion is the Traefik binary's version, so this chart bump is the only Traefik version PR and no separate image pin is wanted
helm chart pin — openbao/openbao: the `charts:` version, answered by its Helm registry
helm chart pin — concourse/concourse: the chart half of the release whose image tag is pinned on the line below, so both bump in one PR (see packageRules)
image tag pin — concourse/concourse: the `image_tag:` half of the entry above, pinned because an image tag that is not the chart's appVersion runs a binary nobody judged the chart against
pinned binary — helm/helm: the `binaries:` version kubementat execs against a cluster, answered by the helm release stream

pinned binary — helmfile/helmfile, pinned twice in versions.yaml for two consumers: the `binaries:` version kubementat execs and the `ci_image:` version the CI image installs. One depName, so one bump PR carries both edits (see packageRules): the drift this file ended was two copies agreeing by luck.
Tekton release — tektoncd/pipeline: the `tekton:` version that `kmt install` builds its release URLs from
Tekton release — tektoncd/dashboard: the `tekton:` version, applied after Pipelines because it reads that API
Tekton release — tektoncd/triggers: the `tekton:` version, applied last of the three

CI image build arg — the ubuntu base tag at `ci_image: BASE_IMAGE_URL:`. Renovate never saw this tag while it was the default of an unextracted Dockerfile ARG; as a versions.yaml key it bumps like any other image, and the base is where apt's freshness lives.

CI image build arg — the kubectl apt channel at `ci_image: KUBECTL_MINOR_VERSION:`. extractVersion reduces every upstream tag to its minor, so a PR means "a new stable minor is served" and never churns on patches inside the channel the URL already installs.
CI image build arg — the Tekton CLI release at `ci_image: TKN_CLI_VERSION:`: the download URL is built from it, so the key is the whole pin
CI image build arg — the yq release at `ci_image: YQ_VERSION:`
CI image build arg — the helm-diff plugin release at `ci_image: HELM_DIFF_VERSION:`
CI image build arg — the Linkerd edge release at `ci_image: LINKERD_VERSION:`. extractVersion keeps edge-* tags only, so a stable tag never enters the candidate set and reorders the list.
CI image build arg — the Node release the tarball is fetched for at `ci_image: NODE_VERSION:`

CI image build arg — the uv release at `ci_image: UV_VERSION:`, the tool the image installs. The uv dependency in pyproject.toml answers to the native pep621 manager: same tool, two pins, and a bump may want both.

container images at `images:` — each value is one whole repo:tag reference, and each match captures depName and tag so one entry covers the block and a bump rewrites only the tag. The repository and the channel suffixes stay as the file wrote them: -rootless belongs to the buildkit tag, -alpine selects the nginx channel, and a newer Maven version means a new -openjdk suffix that the reviewer lines up.
end-to-end harness — the k3s version at `e2e: k3s:`. The +k3sN suffix is valid semver build metadata, so semver-coerced orders it without help.

packageRules.description: minor and patch chart bumps grouped into one branch; majors keep their own branch because the values layers that answer them are edited per release.

Concourse is pinned twice for one release, on two adjacent versions.yaml lines: the chart and the image tag that is the chart's appVersion. Grouping the two puts both edits in one branch, so a bump cannot land a new chart over an old binary or the other way round. The image candidate Renovate proposes is the newest published tag, not the new chart's appVersion — so a Concourse bump PR is only right when the tag it writes equals that appVersion, and the reviewer sets it there.

helmfile is pinned twice under one depName — the runtime binary and the CI image build arg — so grouping gives one bump PR for both. Two deps with the same depName would otherwise compete for the same branch, and moving only one is the drift the central file ended.

the ansible manager mis-fires on this tree's Tekton YAML, reading container images as ansible tasks — 26 dependencies that are not dependencies. Verified by a dry run after the central file landed; the mis-fire is the manager's, not the tree's, so it stays disabled.

the pyenv manager reads `.python-version` (the 3.9 floor the package declares) and would bump it to the newest release. A floor is not a freshness pin — raising it is a compatibility decision that belongs to the Python distribution's own change — so there is nothing for this manager to keep fresh here.

the dockerfile manager has nothing to own since the central file landed: the CI image's `FROM` lines are ARG-driven, so every version it could read arrives from versions.yaml at build time, and the 20 dependencies it still extracts from the file resolve to no branch. Disabling it removes the extraction noise without removing a single real lookup.

the helm-values manager finds image repositories without tags in the shipped values files, because the charts name their images in keys the manager does not pair with a version, or the tag is an env knob. Those reads become tagless dependencies that can never resolve; the images that do carry versions live in versions.yaml. All values files, not just Concourse's — the same shape appears in each.
